# Data Model: Personal Bookmark Manager

**Date**: 2026-09-17  
**Database**: SQLite with foreign keys, WAL, and ordered migrations

## Modeling Rules

- Integer primary keys are internal identifiers; user-facing meaning lives in explicit fields.
- UTC timestamps use one consistent sortable representation and are generated by the server.
- Boolean values are stored as `0` or `1` with `CHECK` constraints.
- User-facing spelling is preserved separately from normalized uniqueness/search keys.
- All foreign-key child columns used by cascades are indexed.
- Bookmark, tag, FTS, saved-view, and selection changes that form one user action commit in one transaction.

## Bookmark

Represents one unique saved web destination.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Primary key |
| `address` | text | Trimmed valid HTTP(S) destination retained for display/opening |
| `normalized_address` | text | Required, unique across active and archived bookmarks; derived by FR-005 rules |
| `address_revision` | integer | Starts at 1 and increments whenever the address changes; guards metadata races |
| `title` | text | Required display value; retrieved, user-authored, or address-derived fallback |
| `title_sort_key` | text | Required Unicode-normalized, case-folded title used for deterministic title ordering |
| `title_provenance` | enum | `fallback`, `retrieved`, or `user` |
| `retrieved_title_candidate` | nullable text | Latest retrieved alternative when a user title must not be overwritten |
| `description` | text | May be empty; retrieved or user-authored |
| `description_provenance` | enum | `fallback`, `retrieved`, or `user` |
| `retrieved_description_candidate` | nullable text | Latest retrieved alternative when a user description must not be overwritten |
| `icon_hash` | nullable text | Foreign key to a validated app-origin PNG; null uses the placeholder |
| `metadata_status` | enum | `pending`, `complete`, `partial`, `failed`, or `skipped_unsafe` |
| `metadata_error_code` | nullable enum | Friendly category such as timeout, denied destination, unsupported content, too large, or unavailable |
| `metadata_fetched_at` | nullable timestamp | Completion time of the last applicable attempt |
| `note_markdown` | text | Canonical user-authored note; empty by default |
| `note_plain` | text | Derived visible text used by search |
| `is_favorite` | boolean | Independent of reading/archive state; false by default |
| `is_unread` | boolean | True means Read Later; false by default |
| `archived_at` | nullable timestamp | Null means active; non-null means archived |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Immutable creation time |
| `updated_at` | timestamp | Refreshed by user-visible content/state changes and applied metadata |

### Bookmark Invariants

- `normalized_address` has a unique index. Application pre-checks improve UX; the constraint resolves races.
- A bookmark is in Read Later only when `is_unread = 1 AND archived_at IS NULL`.
- Archiving changes only `archived_at`; it never clears favorite or unread state.
- Restoring clears `archived_at`, so a retained unread bookmark reappears in Read Later.
- A metadata result may update a row only when its captured `address_revision` still equals the current value.
- A metadata result may update title or description only when that field's provenance is not `user`.
- Changing an address first checks uniqueness. On conflict, the edited bookmark remains unchanged.
- `note_plain` and the search index update in the same transaction as `note_markdown`.
- `title_sort_key` updates in the same transaction as `title` and title sorting uses `id` as the final tie-breaker.

### Bookmark State Transitions

```text
Reading:  read <──────────────> unread / Read Later
Archive:  active ─────────────> archived
          archived ───────────> active

Metadata: pending ────────────> complete
          pending ────────────> partial
          pending ────────────> failed
          pending ────────────> skipped_unsafe
          any non-pending ────> pending (address change or explicit refresh)

Deletion: active or archived ─> permanently removed
```

Reading and favorite transitions are independent from archive transitions.

## Bookmark Icon

Stores a safe, deduplicated site icon served only from the app origin.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `content_hash` | text | Primary key generated from re-encoded bytes |
| `png_bytes` | blob | Validated, bounded, re-encoded PNG only |
| `width` | integer | Positive and within the configured icon bound |
| `height` | integer | Positive and within the configured icon bound |
| `byte_length` | integer | Positive and within the configured transfer/storage bound |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Cache creation time |

An icon row may be referenced by many bookmarks. Unreferenced icons may be removed by maintenance; losing an icon never loses a bookmark and falls back to the placeholder.

## Tag

Represents a reusable flat label.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Primary key |
| `display_name` | text | Trimmed user-facing spelling |
| `name_key` | text | Unicode-normalized, whitespace-normalized, case-folded unique key |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Creation time |

`name_key` is unique. A repeated spelling variant resolves to the existing tag.

## Bookmark Tag

Many-to-many relationship between bookmarks and tags.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `bookmark_id` | integer | Foreign key to Bookmark, cascade on delete |
| `tag_id` | integer | Foreign key to Tag, cascade on delete |

The composite `(bookmark_id, tag_id)` is the primary key. An index on `(tag_id, bookmark_id)` supports exact tag expressions, multi-tag filters, and bulk tag actions. Tags left with no bookmark may be garbage-collected, but saved views preserve their own tag keys.

## Saved View

Stores live search/filter criteria, never bookmark result identifiers.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | Primary key |
| `display_name` | text | Trimmed non-empty user-facing name |
| `name_key` | text | Unicode-normalized, case-folded unique key |
| `query_text` | text | Original validated search expression |
| `grammar_version` | integer | Starts at 1; migration point for future syntax changes |
| `scope` | enum | `active`, `read_later`, or `archived` |
| `favorite_filter` | nullable boolean | Null means any |
| `unread_filter` | nullable boolean | Null means any; scope rules still apply |
| `sort_order` | enum | `created_desc`, `created_asc`, `updated_desc`, or `title_asc` |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Creation time |
| `updated_at` | timestamp | Last rename or criteria update |

`name_key` is unique. The search expression must parse successfully before create/update. Opening a saved view reparses and evaluates current data.

## Saved View Tag

Stores one required tag filter for a saved view.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `saved_view_id` | integer | Foreign key to Saved View, cascade on delete |
| `tag_key` | text | Preserved normalized tag criterion |
| `display_name` | text | Last saved display label |

The composite `(saved_view_id, tag_key)` is the primary key. `tag_key` deliberately does not reference the live Tag table: deleting the last use of a tag leaves the saved criterion intact and produces the specified editable empty result.

## Selection Set

An expiring, non-user-content snapshot used for safe bulk actions.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | Opaque random token primary key |
| `criteria_hash` | text | Hash of the view state that produced the selection |
| `selected_count` | integer | Count shown for confirmation |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Snapshot time |
| `expires_at` | timestamp | Short expiry; abandoned sets are deleted on startup and periodically |

Selection sets are not restored as user state after expiration and do not appear in backups as meaningful content.

## Selection Item

Materializes selection membership.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `selection_id` | text | Foreign key to Selection Set, cascade on delete |
| `bookmark_id` | integer | Foreign key to Bookmark, cascade on delete |

The composite `(selection_id, bookmark_id)` is the primary key. An index on `bookmark_id` supports cascades. A view change deletes the current set; a bulk action consumes and deletes it in the same transaction.

## Bookmark Search Index

A contentful FTS5 virtual table whose `rowid` equals `bookmarks.id`.

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| `title` | Search-normalized title |
| `address` | Search-normalized destination address |
| `description` | Search-normalized description |
| `note_plain` | Search-normalized visible note text |

The table uses the trigram tokenizer over already case-normalized text. Tags stay relational. Bookmark and FTS rows are inserted, updated, and deleted in one transaction, and integrity is checked in migration/maintenance tests.

## Schema Migration

Tracks ordered, immutable SQL migrations.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | integer | Primary key |
| `name` | text | Migration label |
| `applied_at` | timestamp | Successful application time |

Startup applies pending migrations transactionally before the server reports ready.

## Index Plan

- Unique: `bookmarks(normalized_address)`
- Listing: `(archived_at, created_at, id)`, `(archived_at, updated_at, id)`, `(archived_at, title_sort_key, id)`
- Status: `(archived_at, is_unread, created_at, id)`, `(archived_at, is_favorite, created_at, id)`
- Tags: unique `tags(name_key)`, `bookmark_tags(tag_id, bookmark_id)`, and its primary key
- Saved views: unique `saved_views(name_key)`, `saved_view_tags(tag_key, saved_view_id)`
- Selections: primary membership key and `selection_items(bookmark_id)`

The implementation must verify these with representative `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` output and the approved elapsed-time acceptance tests rather than relying on index presence alone.
# Technical Research: Personal Bookmark Manager

**Date**: 2026-09-17  
**Status**: Complete — all planning unknowns resolved

## 1. Runtime and Application Shape

**Decision**: Use a single TypeScript 7/Node.js 24 package with React 19 and Vite 8 for the client and Fastify 5 for the same-origin API and production static server.

**Rationale**: The product is one interactive web application with no SEO or server-rendering requirement. A single production process minimizes operational complexity, while the client/server/shared source split preserves clear boundaries. Fastify provides schema validation and injection testing; Vite produces a static client bundle; Node 24 matches the supplied runtime.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Next.js or a React Router framework: unnecessary SSR and framework lifecycle complexity for a private single-screen application.
- Express: viable, but requires more assembly for schemas, response validation, and injection-style integration tests.
- Separate frontend and backend packages: useful at organizational scale, but adds build and dependency overhead without improving this single deployment.

## 2. API Schemas and Persistence

**Decision**: Define shared TypeBox schemas and use direct, parameterized SQL through `better-sqlite3` 13. Store all durable state in one migrated SQLite database.

**Rationale**: TypeBox 1.x supports the selected TypeScript line and lets Fastify validate JSON while sharing inferred DTO types with the client. Direct SQL keeps complex search-set composition and set-based bulk mutations explicit. SQLite fits one local user and supports transactions, FTS5, WAL, and database-level uniqueness.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Node's built-in `node:sqlite`: attractive, but Node 24 still labels it release-candidate stability.
- Drizzle or Prisma: useful for larger or portable schemas, but add abstraction over the feature's most specialized SQL.
- Browser-only storage: cannot reliably perform server-side metadata retrieval and is less robust for transactional bulk operations and durable migrations.

## 3. Search Grammar and Indexing

**Decision**: Implement a hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser for the approved grammar. Evaluate its AST as bookmark-ID set operations. Use a contentful SQLite FTS5 trigram index for normalized title, address, description, and plain-note text, relational tag predicates, and a scan fallback for search atoms shorter than three characters.

**Rationale**: The grammar has only atoms, implicit/explicit `AND`, and `OR`, so a generator would be disproportionate. Parsing before SQL gives precise source-position errors and prevents SQLite search operators from leaking into the product language. Trigrams satisfy arbitrary substring matching; relational tags preserve exact `#tag` semantics and avoid phrases crossing tag boundaries. The short-term scan is bounded by the approved 10,000-row scale.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Plain `LIKE`/`instr` for every term: simpler, and likely adequate at 10,000 rows, but lacks the same headroom for common substring queries. It remains a fallback if the bundled SQLite lacks the required tokenizer.
- Ordinary word-token FTS: does not meet arbitrary partial matching.
- Passing the query directly to FTS: would accidentally expose unsupported operators and produce inconsistent validation.

## 4. Stable Bulk Selection

**Decision**: Materialize each selection as an expiring server-side selection set and selection-item snapshot. Consume it once in a single bulk-action transaction.

**Rationale**: “Select all” must include off-screen results but must not silently gain or lose items if metadata changes before the action. A snapshot keeps confirmation counts exact, avoids browser payloads containing thousands of identifiers, and supports efficient set-based updates.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Re-run the search criteria when applying the action: small payload, but the affected set can drift after selection.
- Send every identifier from the browser: feasible at 10,000 items, but produces larger requests and weaker count integrity.

## 5. Page Metadata Retrieval

**Decision**: Save with fallbacks immediately, then run a bounded server-side metadata job. Use a dedicated HTTP(S) fetcher with per-hop DNS/IP validation and pinning, manual redirect handling, no credentials/cookies/proxy inheritance, a five-second overall deadline, a one-megabyte decoded HTML limit, and accepted HTML content types only.

**Rationale**: Browser retrieval is unreliable because of cross-origin restrictions. Server retrieval creates an SSRF boundary, so every initial and redirected destination must resolve only to globally routable addresses and the connection must use the already validated answers. Static HTML provides the required metadata without executing untrusted scripts.

**Metadata precedence**:

- Title: non-empty HTML `<title>`, then `og:title`, then address-derived fallback.
- Description: standard meta description, then `og:description`, then empty.
- Icon: declared raster icon candidates, then same-origin `/favicon.ico`, then placeholder.

**Resource policy**: Up to five redirects; stop after document head where possible; trim controls/whitespace; cap title at 512 and description at 2,048 Unicode scalar values; use friendly failure categories.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Headless browser: executes far more untrusted behavior and consumes substantially more resources.
- URL-text or first-IP validation only: vulnerable to alternate DNS answers, redirects, and rebinding.
- Allowing arbitrary custom-port retrieval: broadens the service into a port-probing primitive; custom-port bookmarks can still be stored with fallbacks.

## 6. Site Icon Handling

**Decision**: Fetch icons through the same outbound safety policy, cap transfer at 256 KiB and decoded size at one megapixel, reject SVG/XML/HTML and spoofed types, then resize/re-encode to a small PNG with Sharp and store it under an application-generated content hash.

**Rationale**: Rendering remote icon URLs would contact every saved site from the user's browser and accept tracking, mixed-content, and active-content risks. Re-encoding and same-origin serving give a predictable safe artifact.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Direct remote icon URLs: simplest, but privacy and content-safety behavior is unacceptable.
- Cache verified original raster bytes: lower cost, but retains animation, metadata, and decoder ambiguity.

## 7. Late Metadata and Manual Overrides

**Decision**: Track an address revision/request token and independent title/description provenance (`fallback`, `retrieved`, `user`). A metadata transaction updates only a matching revision and non-user fields; stale results become no-ops, while alternative retrieved values may be offered for explicit acceptance.

**Rationale**: This works across immediate saves, reloads, concurrent tabs, address edits, and out-of-order jobs. Client-only dirty flags do not.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Last response wins: violates the approved no-overwrite behavior.
- Cancel only in the browser: does not survive disconnects or server work already in progress.

## 8. Address and Name Normalization

**Decision**: Use the WHATWG URL parser, retain the entered destination for display/opening, and derive the exact database uniqueness key approved in FR-005. Normalize tag and saved-view keys with whitespace cleanup, Unicode normalization, and locale-independent lowercase, while preserving display spelling.

**Rationale**: An application pre-check provides friendly navigation, while a unique database index closes concurrent races. Application-derived Unicode keys avoid SQLite's ASCII-only built-in case folding.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Redirect or page-canonical identity: would merge aliases and short links explicitly excluded by the specification.
- SQLite `NOCASE` alone: insufficient for general Unicode.

## 9. Formatted Notes

**Decision**: Store Markdown source, derive visible plain text through an AST for search, and render via react-markdown with raw HTML and unsupported node types disabled. Permit only headings, paragraphs, emphasis, lists, links, inline code, and line breaks; allow safe link protocols only.

**Rationale**: Canonical source remains editable and benefits from future renderer security updates. AST extraction is more accurate than removing punctuation with regular expressions. React rendering with a narrow element/protocol allowlist avoids an HTML injection sink.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Store rendered HTML: persists potentially unsafe output and makes later sanitizer improvements ineffective for old data.
- Rich-text document model: unnecessary for the deliberately small formatting set.

## 10. Test and Delivery Tooling

**Decision**: Use Vitest 5 for unit/integration/component tests, Testing Library for user interaction, Fastify injection with temporary real databases, Playwright 1.61.0 for E2E, and Axe plus manual keyboard checks for accessibility. Use Biome for formatting/linting.

**Rationale**: These layers cover pure rules, transactions, the accessible component surface, and built-system behavior. The exact Playwright pin matches the installed browser revision. Deterministic injected DNS/HTTP fixtures test security without weakening production rules or depending on the public Internet.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Public-site metadata tests: slow and nondeterministic.
- Automated accessibility checks alone: cannot prove focus order, announcements, or full keyboard usability.
- Latest Playwright release: may require browser binaries not present in the runtime image.

# Quickstart and Validation Guide

This guide defines how the completed implementation will be built, run, and verified. Commands become runnable during the implementation phase; no application code exists at the planning gate.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.x and npm 11.x
- The shared Playwright Chromium installation at `/opt/playwright-browsers`
- A writable local `data/` directory for the SQLite database
- Port 4000 available

## Install and Verify

```bash
npm ci
npm run format:check
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
npm run test:performance
npm run build
npm run test:e2e
```

The project pins `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0`; do not download another browser revision.

Expected verification outcomes:

- Pure search, normalization, note, and metadata rules pass unit tests.
- API/SQLite integration tests use isolated temporary databases and deterministic network fixtures.
- The seeded 10,000-bookmark search suite meets the one-second p95 criterion.
- A 1,000-bookmark tag-changing bulk action finishes within ten seconds and changes no out-of-selection row.
- The production build completes before runtime presentation.

## Run the Prepared Application

```bash
npm start
```

The foreground server must:

- apply pending migrations before accepting requests;
- bind to `0.0.0.0:4000`;
- serve the JSON API under `/api` and the built client at `/`;
- mark the loaded application shell with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after initial data has loaded or a valid empty state is visible.

Review from the client environment at `http://maker:4000/`. Automated browser checks use `http://127.0.0.1:4000/`.

After dependencies, tests, and the production build succeed, implementation must create:

```json
{"kind":"application","port":4000,"path":"/","start_command":["npm","start"],"start_cwd":"/work"}
```

at `/work/.harness/app.json`.

## End-to-End Validation

### 1. Address-Only Capture and Duplicate Prevention

1. Paste a deterministic fixture-page address and save immediately without typing a title.
2. Confirm a readable fallback and pending state appear immediately.
3. Confirm title, description, and app-origin icon appear when metadata completes.
4. Edit the title, refresh metadata, and confirm the manual title is not replaced.
5. Paste a normalized equivalent of the same address.
6. Confirm no row is created and the existing bookmark opens in edit mode.
7. Repeat after archiving it; confirm the archived match opens and can be restored.

Metadata E2E uses a deterministic injected fixture provider. Separate integration tests prove the production network policy; the browser suite does not depend on public sites.

### 2. Search, Filters, and Sort

1. Seed records with overlapping fields and tags.
2. Verify ordinary adjacent terms use `AND` across fields.
3. Verify `OR`, quoted phrases, `#tag`, and `#"multiword tag"` against [search-grammar.md](./contracts/search-grammar.md).
4. Select multiple tag filters and confirm every selected tag is required.
5. Combine favorite/read state with search and tags.
6. Verify all four sort orders.
7. Enter unmatched quotes and missing operands; confirm position-aware guidance and no data mutation.

### 3. Read Later and Archive Restoration

1. Mark both favorite and non-favorite bookmarks for Read Later.
2. Confirm both appear in Read Later independently of favorite state.
3. Mark one read and confirm it leaves Read Later but remains active.
4. Archive the other and confirm it leaves Read Later while remaining unread.
5. Restore it and confirm it returns to Read Later with favorite and unread states intact.

### 4. Organization and Formatted Notes

1. Edit title, description, tags, favorite state, and note.
2. Use each supported note construct: heading, bold, italic, ordered list, unordered list, link, and inline code.
3. Confirm rendered output contains only supported elements and visible note text is searchable.
4. Exercise raw HTML, image syntax, and unsafe link fixtures; confirm none creates executable or embedded content.

### 5. Stable Bulk Actions

1. Create a filtered result spanning more than one rendered page.
2. Select all results and record the server-confirmed count.
3. Cause a pending metadata update that would otherwise alter the live result.
4. Apply add/remove tag, favorite/unfavorite, read/unread, archive/restore, and delete actions in isolated cases.
5. Confirm only the original snapshot members change.
6. Change the view with an active selection and confirm the selection clears.
7. Confirm bulk deletion shows the stable count and does nothing when cancelled.

### 6. Individual Edit and Delete

1. Edit every editable field and reload the app.
2. Change the address to one already saved and confirm the edited row keeps its old address while the existing match opens.
3. Cancel deletion and confirm no change.
4. Confirm deletion and verify the bookmark disappears from all scopes and live saved-view results.

### 7. Saved Views

1. Configure query, multiple tags, status filters, scope, and sort.
2. Save with a unique name, then change the collection.
3. Reopen the saved view and confirm the criteria are restored against current data.
4. Rename and update it.
5. Remove the last use of a referenced tag and confirm the view remains editable with an empty result.
6. Cancel and then confirm saved-view deletion; bookmarks must remain unchanged.

## Accessibility and Responsive Checks

- Complete every core flow using only the keyboard.
- Confirm focus is visible, dialogs trap and restore focus correctly, and status/error changes are announced.
- Run Axe on empty, populated, filtered, detail/edit, saved-view, and bulk-confirmation states.
- Repeat representative workflows at 320 CSS pixels and a standard desktop width with no horizontal page scrolling.
- Verify external bookmark destinations open without replacing the manager.

## Security-Specific Checks

- Confirm metadata requests deny direct and DNS-resolved loopback, private, link-local, multicast, reserved, and cloud-metadata destinations.
- Confirm every redirect and icon candidate is revalidated and DNS-pinned.
- Confirm time, redirect, decoded-byte, media-type, and image-dimension limits abort safely.
- Confirm the browser never requests remote site icons directly.
- Confirm metadata failures expose friendly categories without internal IP addresses or stack traces.
- Confirm all mutation routes reject invalid schemas and inappropriate cross-origin requests.

- JSON API: [openapi.yaml](./contracts/openapi.yaml)

A single production process minimizes operational complexity, while the client/server/shared source split preserves clear boundaries. Fastify provides schema validation and injection testing; Vite produces a static client bundle; Node 24 matches the supplied runtime.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Next.js or a React Router framework: unnecessary SSR and framework lifecycle complexity for a private single-screen application.
- Express: viable, but requires more assembly for schemas, response validation, and injection-style integration tests.
- Separate frontend and backend packages: useful at organizational scale, but adds build and dependency overhead without improving this single deployment.

## 2. API Schemas and Persistence

**Decision**: Define shared TypeBox schemas and use direct, parameterized SQL through `better-sqlite3` 13. Store all durable state in one migrated SQLite database.

**Rationale**: TypeBox 1.x supports the selected TypeScript line and lets Fastify validate JSON while sharing inferred DTO types with the client. Direct SQL keeps complex search-set composition and set-based bulk mutations explicit. SQLite fits one local user and supports transactions, FTS5, WAL, and database-level uniqueness.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Node's built-in `node:sqlite`: attractive, but Node 24 still labels it release-candidate stability.
- Drizzle or Prisma: useful for larger or portable schemas, but add abstraction over the feature's most specialized SQL.
- Browser-only storage: cannot reliably perform server-side metadata retrieval and is less robust for transactional bulk operations and durable migrations.

## 3. Search Grammar and Indexing

**Decision**: Implement a hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser for the approved grammar. Evaluate its AST as bookmark-ID set operations. Use a contentful SQLite FTS5 trigram index for normalized title, address, description, and plain-note text, relational tag predicates, and a scan fallback for search atoms shorter than three characters.

**Rationale**: The grammar has only atoms, implicit/explicit `AND`, and `OR`, so a generator would be disproportionate. Parsing before SQL gives precise source-position errors and prevents SQLite search operators from leaking into the product language. Trigrams satisfy arbitrary substring matching; relational tags preserve exact `#tag` semantics and avoid phrases crossing tag boundaries. The short-term scan is bounded by the approved 10,000-row scale.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Plain `LIKE`/`instr` for every term: simpler, and likely adequate at 10,000 rows, but lacks the same headroom for common substring queries. It remains a fallback if the bundled SQLite lacks the required tokenizer.
- Ordinary word-token FTS: does not meet arbitrary partial matching.
- Passing the query directly to FTS: would accidentally expose unsupported operators and produce inconsistent validation.

## 4. Stable Bulk Selection

**Decision**: Materialize each selection as an expiring server-side selection set and selection-item snapshot. Consume it once in a single bulk-action transaction.

**Rationale**: “Select all” must include off-screen results but must not silently gain or lose items if metadata changes before the action. A snapshot keeps confirmation counts exact, avoids browser payloads containing thousands of identifiers, and supports efficient set-based updates.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Re-run the search criteria when applying the action: small payload, but the affected set can drift after selection.
- Send every identifier from the browser: feasible at 10,000 items, but produces larger requests and weaker count integrity.

## 5. Page Metadata Retrieval

**Decision**: Save with fallbacks immediately, then run a bounded server-side metadata job. Use a dedicated HTTP(S) fetcher with per-hop DNS/IP validation and pinning, manual redirect handling, no credentials/cookies/proxy inheritance, a five-second overall deadline, a one-megabyte decoded HTML limit, and accepted HTML content types only.

**Rationale**: Browser retrieval is unreliable because of cross-origin restrictions. Server retrieval creates an SSRF boundary, so every initial and redirected destination must resolve only to globally routable addresses and the connection must use the already validated answers. Static HTML provides the required metadata without executing untrusted scripts.

**Metadata precedence**:

- Title: non-empty HTML `<title>`, then `og:title`, then address-derived fallback.
- Description: standard meta description, then `og:description`, then empty.
- Icon: declared raster icon candidates, then same-origin `/favicon.ico`, then placeholder.

**Resource policy**: Up to five redirects; stop after document head where possible; trim controls/whitespace; cap title at 512 and description at 2,048 Unicode scalar values; use friendly failure categories.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Headless browser: executes far more untrusted behavior and consumes substantially more resources.
- URL-text or first-IP validation only: vulnerable to alternate DNS answers, redirects, and rebinding.
- Allowing arbitrary custom-port retrieval: broadens the service into a port-probing primitive; custom-port bookmarks can still be stored with fallbacks.

## 6. Site Icon Handling

**Decision**: Fetch icons through the same outbound safety policy, cap transfer at 256 KiB and decoded size at one megapixel, reject SVG/XML/HTML and spoofed types, then resize/re-encode to a small PNG with Sharp and store it under an application-generated content hash.

**Rationale**: Rendering remote icon URLs would contact every saved site from the user's browser and accept tracking, mixed-content, and active-content risks. Re-encoding and same-origin serving give a predictable safe artifact.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Direct remote icon URLs: simplest, but privacy and content-safety behavior is unacceptable.
- Cache verified original raster bytes: lower cost, but retains animation, metadata, and decoder ambiguity.

## 7. Late Metadata and Manual Overrides

**Decision**: Track an address revision/request token and independent title/description provenance (`fallback`, `retrieved`, `user`). A metadata transaction updates only a matching revision and non-user fields; stale results become no-ops, while alternative retrieved values may be offered for explicit acceptance.

**Rationale**: This works across immediate saves, reloads, concurrent tabs, address edits, and out-of-order jobs. Client-only dirty flags do not.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Last response wins: violates the approved no-overwrite behavior.
- Cancel only in the browser: does not survive disconnects or server work already in progress.

## 8. Address and Name Normalization

**Decision**: Use the WHATWG URL parser, retain the entered destination for display/opening, and derive the exact database uniqueness key approved in FR-005. Normalize tag and saved-view keys with whitespace cleanup, Unicode normalization, and locale-independent lowercase, while preserving display spelling.

**Rationale**: An application pre-check provides friendly navigation, while a unique database index closes concurrent races. Application-derived Unicode keys avoid SQLite's ASCII-only built-in case folding.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Redirect or page-canonical identity: would merge aliases and short links explicitly excluded by the specification.
- SQLite `NOCASE` alone: insufficient for general Unicode.

## 9. Formatted Notes

**Decision**: Store Markdown source, derive visible plain text through an AST for search, and render via react-markdown with raw HTML and unsupported node types disabled. Permit only headings, paragraphs, emphasis, lists, links, inline code, and line breaks; allow safe link protocols only.

**Rationale**: Canonical source remains editable and benefits from future renderer security updates. AST extraction is more accurate than removing punctuation with regular expressions. React rendering with a narrow element/protocol allowlist avoids an HTML injection sink.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Store rendered HTML: persists potentially unsafe output and makes later sanitizer improvements ineffective for old data.
- Rich-text document model: unnecessary for the deliberately small formatting set.

## 10. Test and Delivery Tooling

**Decision**: Use Vitest 5 for unit/integration/component tests, Testing Library for user interaction, Fastify injection with temporary real databases, Playwright 1.61.0 for E2E, and Axe plus manual keyboard checks for accessibility. Use Biome for formatting/linting.

**Rationale**: These layers cover pure rules, transactions, the accessible component surface, and built-system behavior. The exact Playwright pin matches the installed browser revision. Deterministic injected DNS/HTTP fixtures test security without weakening production rules or depending on the public Internet.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Public-site metadata tests: slow and nondeterministic.
- Automated accessibility checks alone: cannot prove focus order, announcements, or full keyboard usability.
- Latest Playwright release: may require browser binaries not present in the runtime image.

# Quickstart and Validation Guide

This guide defines how the completed implementation will be built, run, and verified. Commands become runnable during the implementation phase; no application code exists at the planning gate.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.x and npm 11.x
- The shared Playwright Chromium installation at `/opt/playwright-browsers`
- A writable local `data/` directory for the SQLite database
- Port 4000 available

## Install and Verify

```bash
npm ci
npm run format:check
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
npm run test:performance
npm run build
npm run test:e2e
```

The project pins `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0`; do not download another browser revision.

Expected verification outcomes:

- Pure search, normalization, note, and metadata rules pass unit tests.
- API/SQLite integration tests use isolated temporary databases and deterministic network fixtures.
- The seeded 10,000-bookmark search suite meets the one-second p95 criterion.
- A 1,000-bookmark tag-changing bulk action finishes within ten seconds and changes no out-of-selection row.
- The production build completes before runtime presentation.

## Run the Prepared Application

```bash
npm start
```

The foreground server must:

- apply pending migrations before accepting requests;
- bind to `0.0.0.0:4000`;
- serve the JSON API under `/api` and the built client at `/`;
- mark the loaded application shell with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after initial data has loaded or a valid empty state is visible.

Review from the client environment at `http://maker:4000/`. Automated browser checks use `http://127.0.0.1:4000/`.

After dependencies, tests, and the production build succeed, implementation must create:

```json
{"kind":"application","port":4000,"path":"/","start_command":["npm","start"],"start_cwd":"/work"}
```

at `/work/.harness/app.json`.

## End-to-End Validation

### 1. Address-Only Capture and Duplicate Prevention

1. Paste a deterministic fixture-page address and save immediately without typing a title.
2. Confirm a readable fallback and pending state appear immediately.
3. Confirm title, description, and app-origin icon appear when metadata completes.
4. Edit the title, refresh metadata, and confirm the manual title is not replaced.
5. Paste a normalized equivalent of the same address.
6. Confirm no row is created and the existing bookmark opens in edit mode.
7. Repeat after archiving it; confirm the archived match opens and can be restored.

Metadata E2E uses a deterministic injected fixture provider. Separate integration tests prove the production network policy; the browser suite does not depend on public sites.

### 2. Search, Filters, and Sort

1. Seed records with overlapping fields and tags.
2. Verify ordinary adjacent terms use `AND` across fields.
3. Verify `OR`, quoted phrases, `#tag`, and `#"multiword tag"` against [search-grammar.md](./contracts/search-grammar.md).
4. Select multiple tag filters and confirm every selected tag is required.
5. Combine favorite/read state with search and tags.
6. Verify all four sort orders.
7. Enter unmatched quotes and missing operands; confirm position-aware guidance and no data mutation.

### 3. Read Later and Archive Restoration

1. Mark both favorite and non-favorite bookmarks for Read Later.
2. Confirm both appear in Read Later independently of favorite state.
3. Mark one read and confirm it leaves Read Later but remains active.
4. Archive the other and confirm it leaves Read Later while remaining unread.
5. Restore it and confirm it returns to Read Later with favorite and unread states intact.

### 4. Organization and Formatted Notes

1. Edit title, description, tags, favorite state, and note.
2. Use each supported note construct: heading, bold, italic, ordered list, unordered list, link, and inline code.
3. Confirm rendered output contains only supported elements and visible note text is searchable.
4. Exercise raw HTML, image syntax, and unsafe link fixtures; confirm none creates executable or embedded content.

### 5. Stable Bulk Actions

1. Create a filtered result spanning more than one rendered page.
2. Select all results and record the server-confirmed count.
3. Cause a pending metadata update that would otherwise alter the live result.
4. Apply add/remove tag, favorite/unfavorite, read/unread, archive/restore, and delete actions in isolated cases.
5. Confirm only the original snapshot members change.
6. Change the view with an active selection and confirm the selection clears.
7. Confirm bulk deletion shows the stable count and does nothing when cancelled.

### 6. Individual Edit and Delete

1. Edit every editable field and reload the app.
2. Change the address to one already saved and confirm the edited row keeps its old address while the existing match opens.
3. Cancel deletion and confirm no change.
4. Confirm deletion and verify the bookmark disappears from all scopes and live saved-view results.

### 7. Saved Views

1. Configure query, multiple tags, status filters, scope, and sort.
2. Save with a unique name, then change the collection.
3. Reopen the saved view and confirm the criteria are restored against current data.
4. Rename and update it.
5. Remove the last use of a referenced tag and confirm the view remains editable with an empty result.
6. Cancel and then confirm saved-view deletion; bookmarks must remain unchanged.

## Accessibility and Responsive Checks

- Complete every core flow using only the keyboard.
- Confirm focus is visible, dialogs trap and restore focus correctly, and status/error changes are announced.
- Run Axe on empty, populated, filtered, detail/edit, saved-view, and bulk-confirmation states.
- Repeat representative workflows at 320 CSS pixels and a standard desktop width with no horizontal page scrolling.
- Verify external bookmark destinations open without replacing the manager.

## Security-Specific Checks

- Confirm metadata requests deny direct and DNS-resolved loopback, private, link-local, multicast, reserved, and cloud-metadata destinations.
- Confirm every redirect and icon candidate is revalidated and DNS-pinned.
- Confirm time, redirect, decoded-byte, media-type, and image-dimension limits abort safely.
- Confirm the browser never requests remote site icons directly.
- Confirm metadata failures expose friendly categories without internal IP addresses or stack traces.
- Confirm all mutation routes reject invalid schemas and inappropriate cross-origin requests.

**Rationale**: The product is one interactive web application with no SEO or server-rendering requirement. A single production process minimizes operational complexity, while the client/server/shared source split preserves clear boundaries. Fastify provides schema validation and injection testing; Vite produces a static client bundle; Node 24 matches the supplied runtime.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Next.js or a React Router framework: unnecessary SSR and framework lifecycle complexity for a private single-screen application.
- Express: viable, but requires more assembly for schemas, response validation, and injection-style integration tests.
- Separate frontend and backend packages: useful at organizational scale, but adds build and dependency overhead without improving this single deployment.

## 2. API Schemas and Persistence

**Decision**: Define shared TypeBox schemas and use direct, parameterized SQL through `better-sqlite3` 13. Store all durable state in one migrated SQLite database.

**Rationale**: TypeBox 1.x supports the selected TypeScript line and lets Fastify validate JSON while sharing inferred DTO types with the client. Direct SQL keeps complex search-set composition and set-based bulk mutations explicit. SQLite fits one local user and supports transactions, FTS5, WAL, and database-level uniqueness.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Node's built-in `node:sqlite`: attractive, but Node 24 still labels it release-candidate stability.
- Drizzle or Prisma: useful for larger or portable schemas, but add abstraction over the feature's most specialized SQL.
- Browser-only storage: cannot reliably perform server-side metadata retrieval and is less robust for transactional bulk operations and durable migrations.

## 3. Search Grammar and Indexing

**Decision**: Implement a hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser for the approved grammar. Evaluate its AST as bookmark-ID set operations. Use a contentful SQLite FTS5 trigram index for normalized title, address, description, and plain-note text, relational tag predicates, and a scan fallback for search atoms shorter than three characters.

**Rationale**: The grammar has only atoms, implicit/explicit `AND`, and `OR`, so a generator would be disproportionate. Parsing before SQL gives precise source-position errors and prevents SQLite search operators from leaking into the product language. Trigrams satisfy arbitrary substring matching; relational tags preserve exact `#tag` semantics and avoid phrases crossing tag boundaries. The short-term scan is bounded by the approved 10,000-row scale.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Plain `LIKE`/`instr` for every term: simpler, and likely adequate at 10,000 rows, but lacks the same headroom for common substring queries. It remains a fallback if the bundled SQLite lacks the required tokenizer.
- Ordinary word-token FTS: does not meet arbitrary partial matching.
- Passing the query directly to FTS: would accidentally expose unsupported operators and produce inconsistent validation.

## 4. Stable Bulk Selection

**Decision**: Materialize each selection as an expiring server-side selection set and selection-item snapshot. Consume it once in a single bulk-action transaction.

**Rationale**: “Select all” must include off-screen results but must not silently gain or lose items if metadata changes before the action. A snapshot keeps confirmation counts exact, avoids browser payloads containing thousands of identifiers, and supports efficient set-based updates.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Re-run the search criteria when applying the action: small payload, but the affected set can drift after selection.
- Send every identifier from the browser: feasible at 10,000 items, but produces larger requests and weaker count integrity.

## 5. Page Metadata Retrieval

**Decision**: Save with fallbacks immediately, then run a bounded server-side metadata job. Use a dedicated HTTP(S) fetcher with per-hop DNS/IP validation and pinning, manual redirect handling, no credentials/cookies/proxy inheritance, a five-second overall deadline, a one-megabyte decoded HTML limit, and accepted HTML content types only.

**Rationale**: Browser retrieval is unreliable because of cross-origin restrictions. Server retrieval creates an SSRF boundary, so every initial and redirected destination must resolve only to globally routable addresses and the connection must use the already validated answers. Static HTML provides the required metadata without executing untrusted scripts.

**Metadata precedence**:

- Title: non-empty HTML `<title>`, then `og:title`, then address-derived fallback.
- Description: standard meta description, then `og:description`, then empty.
- Icon: declared raster icon candidates, then same-origin `/favicon.ico`, then placeholder.

**Resource policy**: Up to five redirects; stop after document head where possible; trim controls/whitespace; cap title at 512 and description at 2,048 Unicode scalar values; use friendly failure categories.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Headless browser: executes far more untrusted behavior and consumes substantially more resources.
- URL-text or first-IP validation only: vulnerable to alternate DNS answers, redirects, and rebinding.
- Allowing arbitrary custom-port retrieval: broadens the service into a port-probing primitive; custom-port bookmarks can still be stored with fallbacks.

## 6. Site Icon Handling

**Decision**: Fetch icons through the same outbound safety policy, cap transfer at 256 KiB and decoded size at one megapixel, reject SVG/XML/HTML and spoofed types, then resize/re-encode to a small PNG with Sharp and store it under an application-generated content hash.

**Rationale**: Rendering remote icon URLs would contact every saved site from the user's browser and accept tracking, mixed-content, and active-content risks. Re-encoding and same-origin serving give a predictable safe artifact.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Direct remote icon URLs: simplest, but privacy and content-safety behavior is unacceptable.
- Cache verified original raster bytes: lower cost, but retains animation, metadata, and decoder ambiguity.

## 7. Late Metadata and Manual Overrides

**Decision**: Track an address revision/request token and independent title/description provenance (`fallback`, `retrieved`, `user`). A metadata transaction updates only a matching revision and non-user fields; stale results become no-ops, while alternative retrieved values may be offered for explicit acceptance.

**Rationale**: This works across immediate saves, reloads, concurrent tabs, address edits, and out-of-order jobs. Client-only dirty flags do not.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Last response wins: violates the approved no-overwrite behavior.
- Cancel only in the browser: does not survive disconnects or server work already in progress.

## 8. Address and Name Normalization

**Decision**: Use the WHATWG URL parser, retain the entered destination for display/opening, and derive the exact database uniqueness key approved in FR-005. Normalize tag and saved-view keys with whitespace cleanup, Unicode normalization, and locale-independent lowercase, while preserving display spelling.

**Rationale**: An application pre-check provides friendly navigation, while a unique database index closes concurrent races. Application-derived Unicode keys avoid SQLite's ASCII-only built-in case folding.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Redirect or page-canonical identity: would merge aliases and short links explicitly excluded by the specification.
- SQLite `NOCASE` alone: insufficient for general Unicode.

## 9. Formatted Notes

**Decision**: Store Markdown source, derive visible plain text through an AST for search, and render via react-markdown with raw HTML and unsupported node types disabled. Permit only headings, paragraphs, emphasis, lists, links, inline code, and line breaks; allow safe link protocols only.

**Rationale**: Canonical source remains editable and benefits from future renderer security updates. AST extraction is more accurate than removing punctuation with regular expressions. React rendering with a narrow element/protocol allowlist avoids an HTML injection sink.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Store rendered HTML: persists potentially unsafe output and makes later sanitizer improvements ineffective for old data.
- Rich-text document model: unnecessary for the deliberately small formatting set.

## 10. Test and Delivery Tooling

**Decision**: Use Vitest 5 for unit/integration/component tests, Testing Library for user interaction, Fastify injection with temporary real databases, Playwright 1.61.0 for E2E, and Axe plus manual keyboard checks for accessibility. Use Biome for formatting/linting.

**Rationale**: These layers cover pure rules, transactions, the accessible component surface, and built-system behavior. The exact Playwright pin matches the installed browser revision. Deterministic injected DNS/HTTP fixtures test security without weakening production rules or depending on the public Internet.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Public-site metadata tests: slow and nondeterministic.
- Automated accessibility checks alone: cannot prove focus order, announcements, or full keyboard usability.
- Latest Playwright release: may require browser binaries not present in the runtime image.

# Quickstart and Validation Guide

This guide defines how the completed implementation will be built, run, and verified. Commands become runnable during the implementation phase; no application code exists at the planning gate.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.x and npm 11.x
- The shared Playwright Chromium installation at `/opt/playwright-browsers`
- A writable local `data/` directory for the SQLite database
- Port 4000 available

## Install and Verify

```bash
npm ci
npm run format:check
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
npm run test:performance
npm run build
npm run test:e2e
```

The project pins `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0`; do not download another browser revision.

Expected verification outcomes:

- Pure search, normalization, note, and metadata rules pass unit tests.
- API/SQLite integration tests use isolated temporary databases and deterministic network fixtures.
- The seeded 10,000-bookmark search suite meets the one-second p95 criterion.
- A 1,000-bookmark tag-changing bulk action finishes within ten seconds and changes no out-of-selection row.
- The production build completes before runtime presentation.

## Run the Prepared Application

```bash
npm start
```

The foreground server must:

- apply pending migrations before accepting requests;
- bind to `0.0.0.0:4000`;
- serve the JSON API under `/api` and the built client at `/`;
- mark the loaded application shell with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after initial data has loaded or a valid empty state is visible.

Review from the client environment at `http://maker:4000/`. Automated browser checks use `http://127.0.0.1:4000/`.

After dependencies, tests, and the production build succeed, implementation must create:

```json
{"kind":"application","port":4000,"path":"/","start_command":["npm","start"],"start_cwd":"/work"}
```

at `/work/.harness/app.json`.

## End-to-End Validation

### 1. Address-Only Capture and Duplicate Prevention

1. Paste a deterministic fixture-page address and save immediately without typing a title.
2. Confirm a readable fallback and pending state appear immediately.
3. Confirm title, description, and app-origin icon appear when metadata completes.
4. Edit the title, refresh metadata, and confirm the manual title is not replaced.
5. Paste a normalized equivalent of the same address.
6. Confirm no row is created and the existing bookmark opens in edit mode.
7. Repeat after archiving it; confirm the archived match opens and can be restored.

Metadata E2E uses a deterministic injected fixture provider. Separate integration tests prove the production network policy; the browser suite does not depend on public sites.

### 2. Search, Filters, and Sort

1. Seed records with overlapping fields and tags.
2. Verify ordinary adjacent terms use `AND` across fields.
3. Verify `OR`, quoted phrases, `#tag`, and `#"multiword tag"` against [search-grammar.md](./contracts/search-grammar.md).
4. Select multiple tag filters and confirm every selected tag is required.
5. Combine favorite/read state with search and tags.
6. Verify all four sort orders.
7. Enter unmatched quotes and missing operands; confirm position-aware guidance and no data mutation.

### 3. Read Later and Archive Restoration

1. Mark both favorite and non-favorite bookmarks for Read Later.
2. Confirm both appear in Read Later independently of favorite state.
3. Mark one read and confirm it leaves Read Later but remains active.
4. Archive the other and confirm it leaves Read Later while remaining unread.
5. Restore it and confirm it returns to Read Later with favorite and unread states intact.

### 4. Organization and Formatted Notes

1. Edit title, description, tags, favorite state, and note.
2. Use each supported note construct: heading, bold, italic, ordered list, unordered list, link, and inline code.
3. Confirm rendered output contains only supported elements and visible note text is searchable.
4. Exercise raw HTML, image syntax, and unsafe link fixtures; confirm none creates executable or embedded content.

### 5. Stable Bulk Actions

1. Create a filtered result spanning more than one rendered page.
2. Select all results and record the server-confirmed count.
3. Cause a pending metadata update that would otherwise alter the live result.
4. Apply add/remove tag, favorite/unfavorite, read/unread, archive/restore, and delete actions in isolated cases.
5. Confirm only the original snapshot members change.
6. Change the view with an active selection and confirm the selection clears.
7. Confirm bulk deletion shows the stable count and does nothing when cancelled.

### 6. Individual Edit and Delete

1. Edit every editable field and reload the app.
2. Change the address to one already saved and confirm the edited row keeps its old address while the existing match opens.
3. Cancel deletion and confirm no change.
4. Confirm deletion and verify the bookmark disappears from all scopes and live saved-view results.

### 7. Saved Views

1. Configure query, multiple tags, status filters, scope, and sort.
2. Save with a unique name, then change the collection.
3. Reopen the saved view and confirm the criteria are restored against current data.
4. Rename and update it.
5. Remove the last use of a referenced tag and confirm the view remains editable with an empty result.
6. Cancel and then confirm saved-view deletion; bookmarks must remain unchanged.

## Accessibility and Responsive Checks

- Complete every core flow using only the keyboard.
- Confirm focus is visible, dialogs trap and restore focus correctly, and status/error changes are announced.
- Run Axe on empty, populated, filtered, detail/edit, saved-view, and bulk-confirmation states.
- Repeat representative workflows at 320 CSS pixels and a standard desktop width with no horizontal page scrolling.
- Verify external bookmark destinations open without replacing the manager.

## Security-Specific Checks

- Confirm metadata requests deny direct and DNS-resolved loopback, private, link-local, multicast, reserved, and cloud-metadata destinations.
- Confirm every redirect and icon candidate is revalidated and DNS-pinned.
- Confirm time, redirect, decoded-byte, media-type, and image-dimension limits abort safely.
- Confirm the browser never requests remote site icons directly.
- Confirm metadata failures expose friendly categories without internal IP addresses or stack traces.
- Confirm all mutation routes reject invalid schemas and inappropriate cross-origin requests.

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Personal Bookmark Manager API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Same-origin JSON contract for the approved single-user application.
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary
servers:
  - url: /api
security: []
paths:
  /health:
    get:
      summary: Check application readiness
      operationId: getHealth
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Server and migrated database are ready.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [status]
                properties:
                  status:
                    const: ready
        '400':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'

  /metadata/preview:
    post:
      summary: Preview metadata for an address
      operationId: previewMetadata
      description: Begins automatically after a valid address is entered. The client may save independently while this bounded request is pending.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              additionalProperties: false
              required: [address]
              properties:
                address:
                  type: string
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Retrieved metadata or a usable fallback result.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/MetadataPreview'
        '409':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/DuplicateBookmark'
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'

  /bookmarks:
    get:
      summary: List and search bookmarks
      operationId: listBookmarks
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Scope'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Query'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Tags'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Favorite'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Unread'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Sort'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Cursor'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Limit'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Current result page and total result count.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/BookmarkPage'
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/SearchError'
    post:
      summary: Save a bookmark
      operationId: createBookmark
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/BookmarkCreate'
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Bookmark saved; metadata may still be pending.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Bookmark'
        '409':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/DuplicateBookmark'
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'

  /bookmarks/{bookmarkId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/BookmarkId'
    get:
      summary: Get a bookmark
      operationId: getBookmark
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Bookmark detail.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Bookmark'
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'
    patch:
      summary: Update a bookmark
      operationId: updateBookmark
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/BookmarkPatch'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Updated bookmark.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Bookmark'
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'
        '409':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/DuplicateBookmark'
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'
    delete:
      summary: Permanently delete a bookmark
      operationId: deleteBookmark
      description: The client must obtain explicit user confirmation before sending this request.
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Permanently deleted.
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'

  /bookmarks/{bookmarkId}/metadata-refresh:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/BookmarkId'
    post:
      summary: Refresh bookmark metadata
      operationId: refreshBookmarkMetadata
      responses:
        '202':
          description: A revision-guarded metadata refresh was queued.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [bookmarkId, metadataStatus]
                properties:
                  bookmarkId:
                    type: integer
                  metadataStatus:
                    const: pending
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'

  /bookmarks/{bookmarkId}/icon:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/BookmarkId'
    get:
      summary: Get a safe bookmark icon
      operationId: getBookmarkIcon
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Validated app-origin PNG icon.
          headers:
            X-Content-Type-Options:
              schema:
                const: nosniff
          content:
            image/png:
              schema:
                type: string
                contentEncoding: binary
        '404':
          description: Use the client placeholder icon.

  /tags:
    get:
      summary: List tags
      operationId: listTags
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Existing tags and active bookmark counts.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/TagSummary'
        '400':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'

  /selections:
    post:
      summary: Snapshot a bookmark selection
      operationId: createSelection
      description: Snapshots individual IDs or every bookmark matching the current criteria.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              oneOf:
                - type: object
                  additionalProperties: false
                  required: [mode, ids, criteriaHash]
                  properties:
                    mode:
                      const: ids
                    ids:
                      type: array
                      minItems: 1
                      uniqueItems: true
                      items:
                        type: integer
                    criteriaHash:
                      type: string
                - type: object
                  additionalProperties: false
                  required: [mode, criteria, criteriaHash]
                  properties:
                    mode:
                      const: all_results
                    criteria:
                      $ref: '#/components/schemas/SearchCriteria'
                    criteriaHash:
                      type: string
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Stable expiring selection snapshot.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Selection'
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/SearchError'

  /selections/{selectionId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/SelectionId'
    delete:
      summary: Clear a bookmark selection
      operationId: clearSelection
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Selection cleared or already absent.
        '400':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'

  /selections/{selectionId}/actions:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/SelectionId'
    post:
      summary: Apply a bulk action
      operationId: applyBulkAction
      description: Consumes the stable selection in one transaction. The client confirms permanent deletion before requesting it.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/BulkAction'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Selection consumed and action committed.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/BulkResult'
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/SelectionNotFound'
        '409':
          description: Selection expired before it could be consumed.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'

  /saved-views:
    get:
      summary: List saved views
      operationId: listSavedViews
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Saved views ordered by display name.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/SavedView'
        '400':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'
    post:
      summary: Create a saved view
      operationId: createSavedView
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/SavedViewWrite'
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Saved view created.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/SavedView'
        '409':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/DuplicateSavedView'
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/SearchError'

  /saved-views/{savedViewId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/SavedViewId'
    patch:
      summary: Update a saved view
      operationId: updateSavedView
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/SavedViewWrite'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Saved view renamed or criteria replaced atomically.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/SavedView'
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'
        '409':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/DuplicateSavedView'
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/SearchError'
    delete:
      summary: Delete a saved view
      operationId: deleteSavedView
      description: The client must obtain explicit user confirmation before sending this request.
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Saved view deleted without changing bookmarks.
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'

components:
  parameters:
    BookmarkId:
      name: bookmarkId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: integer
    SavedViewId:
      name: savedViewId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: integer
    SelectionId:
      name: selectionId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: string
    Scope:
      name: scope
      in: query
      schema:
        $ref: '#/components/schemas/Scope'
    Query:
      name: q
      in: query
      schema:
        type: string
        default: ''
    Tags:
      name: tag
      in: query
      style: form
      explode: true
      schema:
        type: array
        items:
          type: string
    Favorite:
      name: favorite
      in: query
      schema:
        type: boolean
    Unread:
      name: unread
      in: query
      schema:
        type: boolean
    Sort:
      name: sort
      in: query
      schema:
        $ref: '#/components/schemas/SortOrder'
    Cursor:
      name: cursor
      in: query
      schema:
        type: string
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 100
        default: 50

  responses:
    DuplicateBookmark:
      description: The normalized address already belongs to a bookmark; open it in edit mode.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            allOf:
              - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'
              - type: object
                required: [existingBookmarkId]
                properties:
                  code:
                    const: DUPLICATE_BOOKMARK
                  existingBookmarkId:
                    type: integer
                  existingScope:
                    $ref: '#/components/schemas/Scope'
    DuplicateSavedView:
      description: A case-insensitive normalized name already exists.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            allOf:
              - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'
              - type: object
                properties:
                  code:
                    const: DUPLICATE_SAVED_VIEW_NAME
                  field:
                    const: name
    ValidationError:
      description: Request fields are invalid.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'
    SearchError:
      description: Search syntax or criteria are invalid.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/SearchProblem'
    NotFound:
      description: Resource not found.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'
    SelectionNotFound:
      description: Selection not found or already consumed.
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'

  schemas:
    Scope:
      type: string
      enum: [active, read_later, archived]
      default: active
    SortOrder:
      type: string
      enum: [created_desc, created_asc, updated_desc, title_asc]
      default: created_desc
    MetadataStatus:
      type: string
      enum: [pending, complete, partial, failed, skipped_unsafe]
    Provenance:
      type: string
      enum: [fallback, retrieved, user]
    Tag:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, name]
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
        name:
          type: string
    TagSummary:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Tag'
        - type: object
          required: [activeBookmarkCount]
          properties:
            activeBookmarkCount:
              type: integer
              minimum: 0
    Bookmark:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required:
        - id
        - address
        - title
        - titleProvenance
        - description
        - descriptionProvenance
        - iconUrl
        - metadataStatus
        - noteMarkdown
        - tags
        - favorite
        - unread
        - archived
        - createdAt
        - updatedAt
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
        address:
          type: string
          format: uri
        title:
          type: string
        titleProvenance:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Provenance'
        retrievedTitleCandidate:
          type: [string, 'null']
        description:
          type: string
        descriptionProvenance:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Provenance'
        retrievedDescriptionCandidate:
          type: [string, 'null']
        iconUrl:
          type: [string, 'null']
        metadataStatus:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/MetadataStatus'
        metadataErrorCode:
          type: [string, 'null']
        noteMarkdown:
          type: string
        tags:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Tag'
        favorite:
          type: boolean
        unread:
          type: boolean
        archived:
          type: boolean
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        updatedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
    BookmarkCreate:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [address]
      properties:
        address:
          type: string
        title:
          type: string
          description: Omit unless the user manually overrides the automatic/fallback title.
        description:
          type: string
          description: Omit unless the user manually overrides the automatic description.
        noteMarkdown:
          type: string
          default: ''
        tags:
          type: array
          uniqueItems: true
          items:
            type: string
        favorite:
          type: boolean
          default: false
        unread:
          type: boolean
          default: false
    BookmarkPatch:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      minProperties: 1
      properties:
        address:
          type: string
        title:
          type: string
        description:
          type: string
        noteMarkdown:
          type: string
        tags:
          type: array
          uniqueItems: true
          items:
            type: string
        favorite:
          type: boolean
        unread:
          type: boolean
        archived:
          type: boolean
        acceptRetrievedTitle:
          type: boolean
        acceptRetrievedDescription:
          type: boolean
    MetadataPreview:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [address, status, fallbackTitle, title, description, iconAvailable]
      properties:
        address:
          type: string
        status:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/MetadataStatus'
        fallbackTitle:
          type: string
        title:
          type: string
        description:
          type: string
        iconAvailable:
          type: boolean
        errorCode:
          type: [string, 'null']
    BookmarkPage:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [items, total, nextCursor]
      properties:
        items:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Bookmark'
        total:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
        nextCursor:
          type: [string, 'null']
    SearchCriteria:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [scope, query, tags, sort]
      properties:
        scope:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Scope'
        query:
          type: string
        tags:
          type: array
          uniqueItems: true
          items:
            type: string
        favorite:
          type: [boolean, 'null']
        unread:
          type: [boolean, 'null']
        sort:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/SortOrder'
    Selection:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, selectedCount, criteriaHash, expiresAt]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
        selectedCount:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
        criteriaHash:
          type: string
        expiresAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
    BulkAction:
      oneOf:
        - type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [type, tags]
          properties:
            type:
              enum: [add_tags, remove_tags]
            tags:
              type: array
              minItems: 1
              uniqueItems: true
              items:
                type: string
        - type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [type]
          properties:
            type:
              enum: [favorite, unfavorite, mark_unread, mark_read, archive, restore, delete]
    BulkResult:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [selectedCount, processedCount, changedCount]
      properties:
        selectedCount:
          type: integer
        processedCount:
          type: integer
        changedCount:
          type: integer
    SavedViewWrite:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/SearchCriteria'
        - type: object
          required: [name]
          properties:
            name:
              type: string
              minLength: 1
    SavedView:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/SavedViewWrite'
        - type: object
          required: [id, grammarVersion, createdAt, updatedAt]
          properties:
            id:
              type: integer
            grammarVersion:
              const: 1
            createdAt:
              type: string
              format: date-time
            updatedAt:
              type: string
              format: date-time
    Problem:
      type: object
      required: [code, message]
      properties:
        code:
          type: string
        message:
          type: string
        field:
          type: string
    SearchProblem:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'
        - type: object
          required: [start, end, hint]
          properties:
            start:
              type: integer
              minimum: 0
            end:
              type: integer
              minimum: 0
            hint:
              type: string
